title: Printer Wall Shelf Ideas: Heights, Mounting, No-Drill Options and Paper Storage for a Clear Desk
seoTitle: Printer Wall Shelf Ideas to Free Up Your Desk
excerpt: Printer wall shelf ideas: measure the printer open and closed, mount a rated shelf at a comfortable height, try risers or corner units if you cannot drill, and store paper flat in a dry cabinet.
imageCaption: A chrome three-tier wire shelving rack with four posts and black feet on a white background. Photo: Sesoris product catalog.
content: The best **printer wall shelf ideas** get the printer off your desk without making it hard to use. Mount a sturdy shelf at a height where you can open the lid and pull out the paper tray, make sure it is rated for the printer's weight and anchored properly, leave space around the vents and cables, and keep paper and ink nearby in closed storage rather than right next to the machine. If drilling is not an option, a small riser, a corner shelf unit or a compact rack can do the same job.

Home printers are awkward. They are too big to ignore, used too rarely to deserve prime desk space and too heavy to put just anywhere. A wall shelf solves most of that, freeing the desk while keeping the printer within reach. This guide covers where to put a printer shelf, how to size and mount it, alternatives if you rent, and how to store paper, ink and cables so the whole setup stays tidy.
## Why Put a Printer on a Wall Shelf
A printer on the desk takes up space you use every day for a machine you might use once a week. Moving it to a wall shelf brings a few benefits:

- **More desk space** for a keyboard, notebook or second monitor.
- **Less clutter**, since the paper tray and output tray no longer hang over your work area.
- **Better access** for everyone in the house if the shelf is in a shared spot such as a hallway nook or office corner.
- **A defined home** for printer supplies, so ink and paper do not drift into other drawers.
The trade-off is that a shelf needs careful sizing and mounting. Printers are heavier than they look, and they need space to open.
## Measure the Printer Before You Choose a Shelf
Before you buy or build anything, measure the printer in every state it will be used:

1. **Closed footprint:** width and depth with all trays folded.
2. **Open depth:** with the paper tray and output tray fully extended.
3. **Open height:** with the scanner lid raised, if it has one.
4. **Weight:** check the manual or the manufacturer's spec sheet.

The shelf needs to be at least as deep as the printer's base, and the space above it must allow the lid to open fully. Many people measure only the closed size, then find the scanner lid hits the shelf or cabinet above.
Also check your printer's manual for any space it needs around vents and moving parts, because these vary from model to model.
## Printer Shelf Options Compared

| Option | Best for | Install | Things to check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wall-mounted shelf with brackets | Most inkjet and small laser printers | Drill into studs or use rated anchors | Shelf depth, load rating, lid clearance |
| Floating shelf | Light, compact printers | Hidden brackets into studs | Floating shelves often have lower load limits |
| Corner shelf unit | Small rooms and unused corners | Freestanding or wall-mounted | Shelf depth at the front edge of a quarter circle |
| Desk riser | Small printers on or beside a desk | Freestanding | Platform size and weight rating |
| Small shelving rack | Printer plus supplies in one unit | Freestanding | Shelf rating, stability, anchoring if tall |
| Cabinet or closet shelf | Hiding the printer when not in use | Existing furniture | Ventilation, door clearance, cable route |
## Pick the Right Height
The best height is one where you can reach the controls, open the lid and load paper without stretching or bending deeply.

- **Standing use:** a shelf at around waist to chest height works well for most adults, so you can see the control panel and lift the lid.
- **Seated use:** if you print from a desk chair, a shelf just above the desk surface, to one side, keeps it within arm's reach.
- **Shared household:** choose a height everyone who uses the printer can reach comfortably.
Avoid mounting the printer high above head height. Lifting a full printer down for maintenance or paper jams becomes awkward and unsafe.
## Mount the Shelf Securely
A loaded printer, plus a ream of paper on top, puts real weight on a shelf. Mounting it properly is the most important step.

- **Find wall studs** and fix brackets into them wherever possible.
- **If you cannot hit studs**, use wall anchors rated for more than the total load, and follow the anchor manufacturer's instructions.
- **Check the shelf's own load rating**, not just the brackets.
- **Use a level** so the printer sits flat. A tilted printer can feed paper unevenly.
- **Leave space at the back** for the power cord and cables.

If you rent or prefer not to drill, consider a freestanding option instead. Tall freestanding units should still be secured. Health Canada advises using anti-tip devices such as angle braces or safety straps to anchor furniture to the wall, and placing heavier items in lower drawers so furniture does not become top-heavy ([Health Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/household-products/furniture-appliance-television-tip-overs.html)).
Our [office wall shelf ideas](/blog/office-wall-shelf-ideas) and [home office wall organization systems](/blog/home-office-wall-organization-systems) cover more shelf and rail layouts.
## Printer Shelf Ideas for Different Spaces
### Beside the Desk

A shelf mounted just above and to the side of the desk keeps the printer close but off the work surface. Place it on the side of your non-dominant hand so it does not get in the way of writing or using a mouse.
### In a Corner
Corners are often empty in small offices and bedrooms. A corner shelf or a corner shelving unit uses that space for a printer and supplies.
![A silver four-tier quarter-round wire corner shelf, empty, on a white background. Photo: Sesoris product catalog](/images/blog/printer-wall-shelf-ideas-corner-shelf.webp)

The [4-tier corner wire shelf](/product/4-tier-corner-wire-shelf-silver) has four quarter-circle shelves and measures 11.81 x 11.81 x 35.43 inches, with threaded feet that level it on an uneven floor. A unit like this suits printer supplies such as paper packs and ink boxes in a corner next to the desk. Measure the depth of a quarter-circle shelf carefully before placing a printer on it, because the usable depth shrinks toward the edges. Our [corner shelf ideas](/blog/corner-shelf-ideas) show more ways to use corners.
### In a Closet or Cabinet

A printer in a closet or cabinet stays hidden when not in use. Make sure there is enough space around it for ventilation, that the door can stay open while printing, and that you can run the power cord to an outlet. Our [office closet organization ideas](/blog/office-closet-organization-ideas) cover cloffice layouts that include printers.
### In a Shared Hallway or Nook
If several people in the house print, a shelf in a hallway nook or near the kitchen makes the printer easy for everyone to reach without walking into someone's office.
## Raise the Printer Without Drilling
If a wall shelf is not practical, a riser lifts a small printer off the desk surface and creates storage underneath.
![A black perforated metal riser platform with four adjustable legs. Photo: Sesoris product catalog](/images/blog/printer-wall-shelf-ideas-riser.webp)

The [monitor riser with 3 height settings](/product/adjustable-monitor-riser-black) is listed for a monitor, laptop or small printer. The platform measures 14.37 x 9.05 inches and has 160 ventilation holes, the legs set to 3.93, 4.73 or 5.52 inches, and the supplier rates it at 44 pounds. Check that your printer's base fits on the platform. The space underneath can hold a ream of paper or a tray of supplies. Clear the platform before changing the height, as the listing instructs.
## Use a Small Rack for Printer and Supplies

A compact shelving rack puts the printer and its supplies in one place. The [3-tier wire shelving rack](/product/3-tier-wire-shelving-rack-chrome-12-inch) measures 11.8 x 11.8 x 23.6 inches, and the supplier rates each shelf at 66 pounds. A small printer can sit on the top shelf if it fits the 11.8 inch footprint, with paper and ink below. Check your printer's dimensions first, since many printers are wider than 12 inches.
## Store Paper the Right Way
Paper storage matters more than most people think. Paper absorbs moisture, which can affect how it feeds through the printer.

OKI, a printer manufacturer, advises storing paper inside a cabinet or other dry and dark place, on a flat surface, and lists 20 degrees Celsius and 50 percent relative humidity as storage conditions. It also advises against storing paper directly on the floor, in direct sunlight, near the inside of an exterior wall, on an uneven surface, or near the printer itself, an air conditioner, a heater or a duct, and recommends not unwrapping paper until just before you use it ([OKI](https://www.oki.com/printing/online-manuals-12/458222/id/contents/contents/kt_000015.html)).
In practice:

- **Keep backstock paper in a closed cabinet or bin**, flat, away from heaters and windows.
- **Load only what you need** into the printer tray.
- **Keep opened reams wrapped** until you use them.
- **Do not stack paper on top of the printer** for long periods.
![A four-tier white storage cabinet with translucent brown front doors and wheels, on a white background. Photo: Sesoris product catalog](/images/blog/printer-wall-shelf-ideas-cabinet.webp)

A closed cabinet near the printer keeps paper dry and dark. The [folding storage cabinet with wheels](/product/folding-storage-cabinet-4-tier-wheels-small) stacks four bins with magnetic front doors, so you can reach the lower tiers without unstacking. Each bin holds about 19 quarts, and the small size measures 15.35 x 11.02 x 33.07 inches with wheels. One tier can hold paper flat, another ink and toner boxes, and the rest can hold envelopes and labels.
## Organize Ink, Toner and Small Supplies
Ink cartridges and toner are expensive, so store them where you will find them.

- **Keep cartridges in their original packaging** until you need them.
- **Store them flat or as the packaging directs**, in a cool, dry spot.
- **Group by printer** if you have more than one.
- **Write the purchase date** on the box so you use older stock first.
![Four black mesh trays stacked, with the long tray and two small trays sitting on the large tray. Photo: Sesoris product catalog](/images/blog/printer-wall-shelf-ideas-mesh-trays.webp)

Small supplies such as staples, paper clips, labels and USB cables are easier to find in divided trays. The [mesh desk drawer organizer set](/product/mesh-desk-drawer-organizer-4-piece-black) includes four trays, one large, one long and two small, that sit side by side in a drawer or stack on a desktop with the three smaller trays resting on the large one. On a printer shelf, the stacked trays keep these items in a small footprint. Our [office supplies organization ideas](/blog/office-supplies-organization-ideas) have more ways to sort small supplies.
## Make a Printer Shelf Look Good
A printer is rarely the most attractive thing in a room, but a few touches help the shelf blend in.

- **Match the shelf to the room.** A wood shelf suits a living space or bedroom office, while a metal or white shelf suits a modern workspace.
- **Keep the top of the printer clear.** Stacks of paper and supplies on top make the whole shelf look cluttered and can block the scanner lid.
- **Use one or two matching containers** for supplies beside or below the printer, rather than a mix of boxes and bags.
- **Add a small plant or a framed print** on a nearby shelf, not on the printer shelf itself, to soften the look.
- **Hide the printer behind a cabinet door or curtain** in living areas, if ventilation allows and the door stays open while printing.
If the printer shares a wall with books or decor, put it on the lowest practical shelf and keep lighter items above. That keeps the heaviest object low and gives the wall a balanced look.
## Plan for How Often You Print
How often you print should shape where the printer goes.

- **Daily printing:** keep the printer within arm's reach of your desk, on a side shelf or riser.
- **Weekly printing:** a shelf a few steps away, such as across the room or in a nearby nook, frees desk space without much inconvenience.
- **Occasional printing:** a closet, cabinet or hallway shelf works well, as long as you can reach it easily when you need it.
Be honest about your habits. A printer used twice a month does not need prime space next to your keyboard.
## Manage Cables Around a Wall Shelf
A floating printer with a cable dangling down the wall looks messy. Plan the cable route before you mount the shelf.

- **Mount the shelf near an outlet** so the power cord does not cross the room.
- **Use a wireless connection** if your printer supports it, to avoid a USB cable to the desk.
- **Run cables down the wall** in a cable raceway painted to match the wall.
- **Leave slack** so you can pull the printer forward to clear paper jams.
Our [desk cable management ideas](/blog/desk-cable-management-ideas) cover raceways, clips and under-desk trays.
## Keep the Printer Easy to Maintain
A wall shelf should not make maintenance harder.

- **Leave room to pull the printer forward** for jams and cleaning.
- **Make sure the cartridge door can open fully** on the shelf.
- **Dust the shelf and the printer** regularly, as dust on a high shelf is easy to forget.
- **Keep the manual or a link to it** with your supplies.
## Common Printer Shelf Mistakes

- **Measuring only the closed printer**, so the lid or trays do not have room to open.
- **Using a shelf or anchors not rated for the load.**
- **Mounting the printer too high** to reach comfortably.
- **Blocking vents** with walls, cabinet sides or stacked paper.
- **Storing paper right next to the printer**, a heater or a window.
- **Leaving no slack in the cables**, so the printer cannot be pulled forward.

If your whole office needs a reset, our [small home office organization ideas](/blog/small-home-office-organization-ideas) and [how to set up a home office desk](/blog/how-to-set-up-home-office-desk-step-by-step-tutorial-2026) guide help plan the rest of the space.
## Frequently Asked Questions
**Q: Can I put a printer on a wall shelf?**
Yes, as long as the shelf and its brackets or anchors are rated for the printer's weight, the shelf is deep enough for the base and there is room above for the lid to open.
**Q: How high should a printer shelf be?**
Choose a height where you can reach the controls, open the lid and load paper comfortably, usually around waist to chest height when standing or just above desk height when seated.
**Q: How deep should a printer shelf be?**
At least as deep as the printer's base. Measure with the trays folded and extended, and make sure the paper tray can open without hitting anything.
**Q: Where should I store printer paper?**
OKI advises storing paper flat in a cabinet or other dry, dark place, away from direct sunlight, exterior walls, heaters, ducts and the printer itself, and keeping it wrapped until use.
**Q: What can I use instead of a wall-mounted printer shelf?**
A desk riser for small printers, a corner shelf unit, a compact shelving rack or a cabinet or closet shelf with enough ventilation.
**Q: Do I need to anchor a freestanding printer rack?**
Tall freestanding units should be anchored. Health Canada advises using anti-tip devices such as angle braces or safety straps to anchor furniture to the wall.
**Q: How do I hide printer cables on a wall shelf?**
Mount the shelf near an outlet, use a wireless connection if possible, run cables in a raceway down the wall and leave slack so the printer can be pulled forward.
**Q: Can a printer go inside a closed cabinet?**
It can, if there is enough space for ventilation as specified in the printer's manual and the door stays open while printing.
## Final Thoughts

A printer wall shelf frees up your desk and gives the printer a proper home. Measure the printer with its trays and lid open, choose a sturdy shelf at a comfortable height and mount it into studs or rated anchors. If drilling is not an option, use a riser, corner unit or compact rack instead. Store paper flat in a dry closed cabinet, keep ink and small supplies in divided trays and plan the cable route before you mount anything. With those details right, the printer stays out of the way until you need it.
